parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe a suitable method for studying the rate of this reaction at a temperature of $40^\circ\text{C}$, given the following.

- a solution of $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ 1-chloro-1-phenylethane, labelled **A**

- a solution of $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ sodium hydroxide, labelled **B**

- $0.10\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ HCl

- volumetric glassware

- ice-cold solvent

- stopclock

- access to standard laboratory equipment and chemicals

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
The rate of this reaction was measured at different initial concentrations of the two reagents.

The table shows the results obtained.

| experiment | $[\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHClCH}_3]$ / $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | $[\text{OH}^-]$ / $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ | relative rate |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1 | 0.05 | 0.10 | 0.5 |
| 2 | 0.10 | 0.20 | 1.0 |
| 3 | 0.15 | 0.10 | 1.5 |
| 4 | 0.20 | 0.15 | to be calculated |

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text: Deduce the order of reaction with respect to each of $[\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CHClCH}_3]$ and $[\text{OH}^-]$. Explain your reasoning.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write the rate equation for this reaction, stating the units of the rate constant, $k$.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Calculate the relative rate for experiment 4.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Use your answers in **(b)(i)** to help you to draw the mechanism for the reaction of 1-chloro-1-phenylethane with hydroxide ions, including the following.

- all relevant lone pairs and dipoles
- curly arrows to show the movement of electron pairs
- the structures of any transition state or intermediate

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text:
This reaction was carried out using a single optical isomer of 1-chloro-1-phenylethane.

Use your mechanism in **(i)** to predict whether the product will be a single optical isomer or a mixture of two optical isomers. Explain your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text:
The proton NMR spectrum of a sample of 1-phenylethanol shows four peaks: a multiplet for the $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$ protons and three other peaks as shown in the table. When the sample is shaken with $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ and the proton NMR spectrum recorded, **fewer** peaks are seen.

Complete the table for the proton NMR spectrum of 1-phenylethanol, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH(OH)CH}_3$.

Use of the *Data Booklet* might be helpful.

| $\delta$ / ppm | number of $^1\text{H}$ atoms responsible for the peak | group responsible for the peak | splitting pattern | result on shaking with $\text{D}_2\text{O}$ |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| 1.4 |  |  |  |  |
| 2.7 |  |  |  |  |
| 4.0 |  |  |  |  |
| 7.2-7.4 | 5 | $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5$ | multiplet | peak remains |
